description: A Game designed to describe space problems.
summary:
Pitch to Orbit is a pixel-art game that teaches kids how real space missions are planned by letting them plan one themselves. Instead of just reading facts, players make the same kinds of choices engineers make.

Players explore a space centre and visit stations that match the real steps of a mission. In the Telescope Lab, every NASA fact is a short mini-game they must win, like cooling the Moon to -173°C or drilling through Europa’s ice to find its hidden ocean. In the Design Bay, they design their spacecraft. At the Sponsor Bank, they pitch four sponsors for funding, and each one explains how much they give and why. In the Parts Factory, they add upgrades and see where each part goes and how it changes the craft. Then they pick a rocket strong enough to lift it, launch, and handle surprises in space like solar storms.

Nine missions unlock one at a time, from low Earth orbit to the Andromeda Galaxy. Every choice is a real trade-off: more upgrades make a craft safer but heavier, and heavier crafts need bigger, more expensive rockets. A step-by-step tutorial helps anyone aged 12 and up, and it runs free in any browser.
details: Pitch to Orbit is a pixel art interactive game, that teaches players how to fund, pitch, upgrade, launch, & prepare for unexpected problems. Everyone in this world is different. And everyone learns differently, so I came up with an idea that actually excites players while also giving them valuable knowledge about NASA. Most people do not have access to resources, and money to build, pitch, and launch a whole spacecraft, let alone kids. I designed a game that virtually connects with future engineers. The intended impact of this project is for every single person, kid or adult to knowhow much effort, and time a real nasa space mission takes. This game also teaches a very valuable life lesson, it is that you never know when you'll start facing unexpected problems in life. Just like when players launch the rocket they have to troubleshoot and think to save their space craft from disaster. Visual Studio Code, Github, HTML, Canva, Claude AI.
